Q: What is the updated text for the front of the Druid?
A: Tap -> Play or draw a site. If this is your first turn, summon Tawny here. Tap -> Summon Bruin here. Flip this card.

title: FAQ: Drums of Doom
text:
Q: I strike your minion, which is nearby the Drums. Then, you redirect the damage to a bodyguard (e.g. Royal Bodyguard, Sir Gawain), who is not nearby the Drums. Does your bodyguard take lethal damage?
A: No. If the minion actually being damaged is not near the Drums, the damage is not Lethal.

title: FAQ: Duplicator
text:
Q: How does this ability impact my collection?
A: You may include any cards you wish in your collection, following normal deckbuilding rules. If you have 0 copies of a unique card in your deck, you may include 1 ))copy(( in your collection. If you have 2 copies of a unique card in your deck, you cannot include any copies in your collection.

title: FAQ: Dwarven Digging Team
text:
Q: If I have Dwarven Digging Team in play, can I choose to summon minions underground without a printed Burrowing ability?
A: No. The units don't gain Burrowing until they're at nearby sites, and you must choose the summoning location when you cast the spell. When you cast the minion spell, it doesn't have burrowing yet, and thus you cannot pick an underground location.

title: FAQ: Earthquake
text:
Q: What does 'normal size' mean?
A: Anything that occupies exactly 1 location.

title: FAQ: East-West Dragon
text:
Q: Does diagonal movement include 'sideways' movement?
A: No.

title: FAQ: Edge of the World
text:
Q: What happens if Edge of the World's ability is lost (e.g. Smokestacks of Gnaak), then Edge of the World gets surrounded by sites, then its ability is regained (e.g. Smokestacks of Gnaak moves away)?
A: In this rare case, Edge of the World would destroy itself.

title: FAQ: Enchantress
text:
Q: Turning auras into minions!? Is this real?
A: Yes, indeed. Enchantress is a very versatile Avatar, and one that twists the rules to create very interesting games. Be sure to check these FAQs as well as the auras you're looking to animate. Since many auras occupy a 2x2 area in the realm, you may want to learn about oversized units as well.

title: FAQ: Entangle Terrain
text:
Q: Does this affect subsurface units, as well as surface?
A: Yes, since it doesn't say 'atop.' Note that it doesn't affect minions in the void, since the void isn't a site.

title: FAQ: Erik's Curiosa
text:
Q: Do I really have to rip it to pieces?
A: Please see the golden rule! The point is to actually, literally rip the card up, so it will never be playable again. It is banished after you rip it.

title: FAQ: Ersatz Platz
text:
Q: How do I resolve this effect?
A: When you would use your avatar's ability (or another ability to play sites without restriction), you may choose to play that site from your collection and banish Ersatz Platz.

title: FAQ: Ether Core
text:
Q: Must one of my units carry this to gain the mana?
A: Yes! If no one is carrying it, it isn't controlled by you. Without a controller, the Ether Core provides mana to no one. Remember that carriable artifacts must be carried to be controlled!

title: FAQ: Evil Presence
text:
Q: The term 'summon' means 'enter the realm.' So, does that mean I can play minions here for free?
A: No. This effect simply provides additional locations where you may summon your minions.

title: FAQ: Evil Twin
text:
Q: Can I summon Evil Twin to a non-surface location if it will be copying a minion that has the appropriate ability (e.g. summon to an underground location while copying a Root Spider)?
A: No. The Evil Twin only gains the abilities as enters the realm, and you must declare its summoning location at the time you cast it, before it enters.

title: FAQ: Failed Mutation
text:
Q: What does 'can't be targeted or damaged by magic' mean?
A: Magic can't target the card and the card can't be damaged by Magic (even without targeting). The card can still be targeted by non-Magic effects.

title: FAQ: Faith Incarnate
text:
Q: Does this effect count all wards in the realm, or only ones I control?
A: It counts all wards in the realm, on any unit or site!

title: FAQ: Falling Star
text:
Q: What does 'When the star falls' mean?
A: At the end of each of your turns, during step 1 of the end phase, add a counter to Falling Star. When you add the third counter, you immediately summon a minion and resolve the rest of this effect, then dispel Falling Star.

title: FAQ: False Idol
text:
Q: Do I draw a spell if my opponent's minion enters the realm tapped?
A: No. This ability only triggers when a minion goes from being untapped to tapped while nearby the Idol.

title: FAQ: Far East Assassin
text:
Q: When you use the ability, what happens to the 'thrown' artifact?
A: It is no longer carried by the Assassin, and is uncontrolled in the target's location. Any unit may pick it up normally (including the Assassin, if it happens to be in that location).

title: FAQ: Feign Death
text:
Q: If I choose a minion that has no Deathrite ability, does it still gain stealth?
A: Yes, it will still gain stealth.

title: FAQ: Fenvale Muse
text:
Q: What happens if I use this to trigger the Genesis ability of a site my opponent controls?
A: The controller of the site will be the one to resolve the Genesis ability. So in the case of a Desert, your opponent will choose the nearby site where damage is dealt. For a River, your opponent will be the one to look at their next spell and choose to put it on the bottom of their spellbook.

title: FAQ: Fey Changeling
text:
Q: Can this be summoned to an inhospitable location (e.g. underground) and die, but still have a chance to use its genesis ability first?
A: No. You cannot choose to summon a minion underground, underwater, or in the void unless it has the appropriate ability.

title: FAQ: Fields of Camlann
text:
Q: What is the proper timing of resolution for this effect?
A: The non-active player chooses a minion, then the active player chooses a minion. Then all other minions are killed. The non-active player resolves any triggered abilities (like deathrite), and finally the active player resolves their triggered abilities.

title: FAQ: Fire Harpoons!
text:
Q: Does the 'adjacent Water site' need to be in the same region as the caster?
A: No. Because the Water site is not targeted, and because the card text uses 'site' instead of 'location,' the site does not need to be in the same region as the caster.

title: FAQ: Firebolts
text:
Q: What does 'one at a time' mean?
A: Resolve the first bolt (including any deathrite or other 'kills' abilities), then resolve the next one, then resolve the 3rd one. Each bolt must go in the same direction.

title: FAQ: Fisherman's Family
text:
Q: Are these family cards of Castle Servants, Common Cottagers, Blacksmith Family, and Fisherman's Family considered Air, Earth, Fire, and Water spells, respectively?
A: Yes. You can see the spell's colored frame matches those elements, so Castle Servants is an Air spell, Common Cottagers is an Earth spell, Blacksmith Family is a Fire spell, and Fisherman's Family is a Water Spell.

title: FAQ: Flagellant
text:
Q: If damage is prevented, do I still heal?
A: No. Flagellant must actually take 1 or more damage for you to heal.

title: FAQ: Flame of the First Ones
text:
Q: What is a 'new site'?
A: A site where this card has not stopped since entering the realm.

title: FAQ: Flame Wave
text:
Q: Can the grid pattern be flipped horizontally?
A: Yes. You pick the leftmost or rightmost column, and that is where the Flame Wave starts.

title: FAQ: Flamecaller
text:
Q: Is the projectile considered fire damage?
A: Yes.

title: FAQ: Flaming Sword
text:
Q: If the attack damage was increased or decreased, does the splash damage include the change?
A: Yes. For example, Critical Strike will splash double damage.

title: FAQ: Flanking Maneuver
text:
Q: Do the locations need to be in the same region?
A: No. Teleport effects ignore regional boundaries unless otherwise specified, and the only restriction on this effect is that the locations be a chess knight's move apart on the board. For example, if A is a void square, and B contains a site, Flanking Maneuver can move units from that void location to either the surface or subsurface of the site.

title: FAQ: Flood
text:
Q: How do Drought and Flood interact?
A: See '((Example - Flood vs. Drought))' in the codex.

title: FAQ: Floodplain
text:
Q: Can Floodplain still flood a site affected by Drought?
A: Yes. See '((Example - Flood vs. Drought))' in the codex.

title: FAQ: Forsaken
text:
Q: Can I cast this onto my opponent's site in an outer column?
A: No, this is an additional casting restriction; it does not allow you to summon Forsaken to locations you normally could not.

title: FAQ: Free City
text:
Q: Can my Free City be struck by opposing units, and if so, will it take damage?
A: Yes, it can be struck, and any strike damage to your Free City will cause your avatar to ))lose(( the same amount of life.

title: FAQ: Frontier Settlers
text:
Q: Can Frontier Settlers play a site that isn't adjacent to your other sites?
A: Yes.

title: FAQ: Frozen Horror
text:
Q: If I activate this ability and then move a minion nearby the Horror, does the minion become disabled?
A: No. This ability disables minions that are nearby the Horror when the ability is activated. A minion moving nearby after that moment will not be disabled.

title: FAQ: Garden of Eden
text:
Q: Does this affect spells drawn by things like Morgana le Fay and the Omphaloi?
A: Yes.  Though those cards end up in another zone, they count as being drawn by the player, and will count against the one spell that can be drawn per turn.   For example, if a player draws a site at the start of their turn and then plays [[Morgana le Fay]], Morgana will only draw 1 spell into her hand, resulting in a total of only 1 spell drawn by that player that turn.  See the Only It Can Cast entry for more information.

title: FAQ: Gargantula
text:
Q: Does tapping to free a trapped minion count as interacting with the realm?
A: Yes, tapping to free a minion from its cocoon is activating a special ability, and counts as interacting with the realm.

title: FAQ: Geomancer
text:
Q: When I play an Earth site using the second ability, do I also place a rubble in an adjacent void?
A: No. You only place a rubble if you play an Earth site using the first ability.

title: FAQ: Geyser
text:
Q: If a unit moves into the site on the same turn, but after Geyser has been cast, does it gain Airborne?
A: No, the minion must be at the site when Geyser resolves to gain Airborne.

title: FAQ: Ghost Ship
text:
Q: If I teleport my Ghost Ship from the void to a site, does its ability trigger?
A: Yes.

title: FAQ: Giant Shark
text:
Q: Will it fight units that are Airborne or Stealthed?
A: Yes. This isn't an attack (which has targeting restrictions), but actually a fight (which simply specifies who fights based on card text).

title: FAQ: Gift of the Raven
text:
Q: Do multiple castings of this stack? Does it stack with other abilities that cause the minion's damage to heal me?
A: Yes, each instance of an effect like this will trigger and heal you independently.

title: FAQ: Gilded Aegis
text:
Q: A minion with Gilded Aegis is on a site chosen for Scorched Earth. The Aegis and the minion are being destroyed simultaneously. Does the Aegis have a chance to save the minion before it's destroyed?
A: Yes.

title: FAQ: Gilman House
text:
Q: Is this effect limited to once per turn?
A: Nope! You may use it as many times as you want in a turn, if you meet the threshold requirement. Of course, in Constructed play, you'll be limited to four, since you can have at most four Horrible Hybrids in your collection.

title: FAQ: Gnome Hollows
text:
Q: If I have Crusade or House Arn Bannermen affecting my Gnome Hollows, may I summon a 2-power minion there?
A: Yes. It's first summoned (enters the realm), then ongoing effects are applied (e.g. Crusade).

title: FAQ: Golden Dawn
text:
Q: How do I resolve this effect?
A: Deal face up to your back row one at a time, placing each card to the surface of a site as you go. Then, shuffle any non-minions and put them on the bottom of your deck. Now all the minions are summoned simultaneously to the location they were dealt to; resolve any effects of those minions being summoned, e.g. genesis effects. Finally, check to see if you're at Death's Door now, and if so, all the summoned minions gain Charge.

title: FAQ: Golgor
text:
Q: Can I choose to banish only some minions from the targeted location?
A: No, if you choose to use this ability you must banish all minions at the targeted location with 2 or less power.

title: FAQ: Grandmaster Wizard
text:
Q: There's a promotional version of this card with the name 'Grandmeowster Wizard.' Since it has a different name, does that mean I can have two copies of each in my deck?
A: No, treat 'Grandmeowster Wizard' as being named 'Grandmaster Wizard' for all deck building and gameplay purposes.

title: FAQ: Grapple Shot
text:
Q: The alpha and beta text is different, which should I use?
A: The Beta text is correct.

title: FAQ: Grasping Ground
text:
Q: Are the minions and artifacts targeted by the allies which drag them down, or by the caster of Grasping Ground?
A: The caster of Grasping Ground must be able to target the minions and artifacts which will be be dragged down by their allies.

title: FAQ: Great Old One
text:
Q: How does Drought interact with Great Old One?
A: These are both passive effects, so whichever was played last takes precedence.

title: FAQ: Great Wall
text:
Q: The foil and non-foil beta cards have different text. Which is correct?
A: The non-foil beta text is correct. You may use a foil beta Great Wall in tournament play (or the alpha version), but it must be played with the non-foil beta text; ensure your opponent knows the proper text when it's played.

title: FAQ: Grigori Rasputin
text:
Q: How do I resolve this ability?
A: Rasputin must be in your cemetery to use this ability. Then, choose the Evil ally you will banish, which may be anywhere and not limited to your own sites. Since Banishing is the cost of the activated ability, resolve the whole activated ability before actually banishing the minion. (This is analogous to the '((Sacrifice))' rules.) Rasputin gains the printed power and abilities of the ally. Resolve Genesis abilities and any 'enter the realm' abilities. Finally, the Banished ally is actually removed from the realm. (Place it under Rasputin as a reminder of the current effect.)

title: FAQ: Grim Reaper
text:
Q: How does this ability work?
A: When Reaper kills a minion, the minion is banished instead of dying. In addition, any copies of that minion in play (regardless of who controls them) are also banished. Finally, you search the owner's library of the minion that was killed (and only that player).

title: FAQ: Grösse Poltergeist
text:
Q: If a unit is carrying the animated artifact, who retains control?
A: When the artifact is animated, it becomes a minion, and thus cannot be carried. The controller of Grösse Poltergeist gets control.

title: FAQ: Guardian Angel
text:
Q: Can you 'fly to' a minion already sharing your location?
A: No, that's not 'flying to.' Summon the Guardian Angel to a different location!

title: FAQ: Guile Sirens
text:
Q: Can it target a unit in a different region?
A: No. Targeting (by default) requires the source and the target to be in the same region.

title: FAQ: Harbinger
text:
Q: Does Harbinger's ability combo with other effects that allow you to cast minions, e.g. Elder Ruins, Troubled Town, Peculiar Port, etc.?
A: Yes! It's effectively a passive ability that can be used whenever you cast a spell on your turn. The golden rule, baby!

title: FAQ: Harpyon Urge
text:
Q: What does 'an ally flies' mean?
A: The chosen unit takes flying steps as if it had the airborne ability. If the unit cannot take steps (due to being immobile, for instance), it cannot move to the targeted minion.

title: FAQ: Haystack
text:
Q: How does this interact with effects like Browse or Kelp Caverns, which do not say to search, but have you look at cards instead?
A: If the effect does not use the word 'search' in its text, it will not be limited by Haystack.

title: FAQ: Headless Haunt
text:
Q: What if my Headless Haunt tries to teleport into an illegal location? (e.g. Gnome Hollows)
A: The teleport effect fails, and it remains where it was.

title: FAQ: Heirloom Lost
text:
Q: What happens to the site that is replaced?
A: The site being replaced is banished.

title: FAQ: Hemogoblet
text:
Q: Can I attempt to fill the Hemogoblet if it's already full?
A: No, you must empty it first.

title: FAQ: Highland Falconer
text:
Q: What does 'shuffle if needed' mean?
A: If you searched your spellbook, shuffle it. If you end up summoning a beast from your hand, you may still have searched your spellbook if you wanted.

title: FAQ: Hillock Basilisk
text:
Q: If I summon a minion to a location affected by Hillock Basilisk, will my minion's Genesis ability resolve?
A: Yes, the minion will not be at rest until all of its events on the storyline are resolved, including its Genesis ability.

title: FAQ: Hillside Chapel
text:
Q: If the allied minion was already tapped before using this ability on them, do they still gain Ward?
A: Yes, you resolve as much of this ability as you can. Granting the Ward is not contingent on the minion being untapped beforehand.

title: FAQ: Horn of Caerleon
text:
Q: If my minion gains charge from the Horn to Move and Attack and then leaves the Horn's range, can it finish the attack?
A: Yes, as the minion has already tapped, the rest of the Move and Attack will resolve. Once a charge has been sounded in the heat of battle, there's no stopping it!

title: FAQ: Horns of Behemoth
text:
Q: Does it turn into a Demon minion?
A: Yes, it becomes a minion with the Demon type, and is no longer a site.

title: FAQ: Hotwheel
text:
Q: Does this strike a unit at the location it was summoned to?
A: No, since it will enter that location before its Genesis ability begins to resolve. It will only strike a unit at each of the two new locations it enters while resolving its Genesis.

title: FAQ: Hounds of Ondaros
text:
Q: What does it mean to 'permanently lose stealth'?
A: Simply remove the stealth token. It does not prevent the minion from gaining stealth later.

title: FAQ: Howl from Beyond
text:
Q: How do I resolve this effect?
A: Deal face up, one at a time. Then, draw the voidwalk minions and Monsters, and banish the rest. No minions actually 'enter' the realm with this effect.

title: FAQ: Hyperparasite
text:
Q: Is the minion only disabled while being carried?
A: Yes, if the minion is no longer carried, it is no longer disabled.

title: FAQ: Ice Lance
text:
Q: If Ice Lance doesn't hit anything at the first location where the projectile appears, and then hits something at the 2nd location, how much damage does it do at that 2nd location?
A: 2 damage at the 2nd location. Ice Lance's damage decreases based on locations the projectile enters, not based on how many things it hits or doesn't hit.

title: FAQ: Ignis Rex
text:
Q: What is a fire card?
A: Fire sites and fire spells are fire cards. See the 'element' codex entry for more details.

title: FAQ: Imperial Road
text:
Q: If I play a Village on my opponent's turn via Imperial Road, can I pay 1 mana to summon a Foot Soldier?
A: The genesis effect triggers, but you don't have any mana available on your opponent's turn, so no.

title: FAQ: Imposter
text:
Q: Can Imposter wear masks of Avatars with pre-game or setup abilities, and if so, what happens?
A: Yes, you can wear masks of those avatars, and you simply ignore their pre-game or setup abilities since the game has already started by the time you put on the mask. For example: You can use [[Pathfinder]]'s ability even though your atlas has duplicate sites. You don't get to pick a Unique Dragon as [[Dragonlord]]. (Probably not a good choice of masks.) You don't roll for summoning portals as [[Harbinger]]. (Probably not a good choice of masks.) Your decks and card sleeves remain as-is for [[Magician]].  (Probably not a good choice of masks.)

title: FAQ: Infiltrate
text:
Q: If my Infiltrated unit attacks my opponent's undefended site, do I retain control of it?
A: No. Once the infiltrated minion no longer has stealth, you ))lose(( control of it.

title: FAQ: Interrogator
text:
Q: When does the enemy avatar have the opportunity to pay life?
A: Immediately after the strike, before deathrites resolve. For example, if your strike puts them to 2 or less life, they will not be able to pay 3 life.

title: FAQ: Into the Abyss
text:
Q: Normally pull effects can't cross regional boundaries. Can I actually pull the target minion into the void?
A: Yes, obviously!

title: FAQ: Iron Shackles
text:
Q: Can I target a burrowed minion or a voidwalk minion?
A: Not unless you have a burrowed spellcaster or a spellcaster in the void. Since the effect uses the word 'target,' the spellcaster must be in the same region as the target. (There are four regions: surface, underground, underwater, void.)

title: FAQ: Ironclad
text:
Q: How does this ability work?
A: Any time your Avatar would take damage, you reduce that damage by 2, to a minimum of 0. Note that an enemy striking one of your sites causes life loss to your Avatar, not damage; life loss is not affected by this ability. Each source of damage is reduced by 2. For example, if you attack and three Foot Soldiers defend together, you take 0 damage since each Foot Soldier would do 1 damage, which you reduce. As another example, if you are hit by an Arcane Barrage for 5, you take 0 damage, since each projectile would do 1 damage, which you reduce.

title: FAQ: Island Leviathan
text:
Q: Does it turn into a Monster minion?
A: Yes. It becomes a minion with the Monster type, and no longer a site.

title: FAQ: Jack the Ripper
text:
Q: Is Jack the Ripper a Monster as well as a Mortal?
A: Yes! The inclusion of the capitalized 'Monstrous' in his typeline makes him a Monster (and thus Evil).

title: FAQ: Jihad
text:
Q: The term 'summon' means 'enter the realm.' So, does that mean I can play minions here for free?
A: No. This effect simply provides additional locations where you may summon your fire minions.

title: FAQ: Joust!
text:
Q: When exactly do the minions fight?
A: After both units have taken their step they will fight from their new locations. If either doesn't move, they haven't passed each other and therefore no joust takes place.

title: FAQ: Kairos the Archivist
text:
Q: How do I 'archive the state of the realm' ?
A: Take a snapshot of the cards in the realm. Players should literally take a picture of it on their phone! If you include this card in your deck, you should be prepared to take a picture during the game. Make additional notes as needed to track things like whether a unit has used its Pick Up and Drop ability for the turn, the controller of a Mesmerized minion, or if there's an ongoing effect on a minion like ))Power(( of Flight. Players are expected to make additional notes as needed to be able to recreate the state of those cards, if a picture alone is insufficient.

title: FAQ: Karkemish Chimera
text:
Q: Units A, B, and C are being attacked; can unit D defend the attack and protect A, B, and C, or just one of them?
A: Just one; you must choose unit A, B, or C to be defended.

title: FAQ: Key to the City
text:
Q: When does this artifact provide mana?
A: When it enters the realm, and at the start of its controller's turn.

title: FAQ: Khamaseen Mummy
text:
Q: What happens if I use this to trigger the Genesis ability of a site my opponent controls?
A: The controller of the site will be the one to resolve the Genesis ability. So in the case of a Desert, your opponent will choose the nearby site where damage is dealt. For a River, your opponent will be the one to look at their next spell and choose to put it on the bottom of their spellbook.

title: FAQ: King Arthur
text:
Q: What happens if King Arthur is in the realm and my opponent would control a card I own?
A: While King Arthur rules the realm, if your opponent would control a card you own, you control it instead (applying equally for both players). For example: My opponent plays [[Lilith]] then summons a minion from my deck. My opponent would normally control a minion they summoned, but I control it while King Arthur is in the realm. I play [[Heirloom Lost]], [[Postern Gate]], [[Desecrate]] to get a [[Desecrated Ground]], etc. My opponent would normally control that site I own, but I control the site while King Arthur is in the realm. I play any Relic (e.g. [[Ring of Morrigan]]) and my opponent takes it somehow (e.g. [[Swap]]). My opponent would normally control that relic while carrying it, but I control it while King Arthur is in the realm. Even if I control it, my opponent's unit is still the bearer and can benefit from bearer abilities. Since I control it, terms like 'ally' and 'enemy' apply from my perspective (the controller). If it's dropped, no one controls it, as normal. I animate my aura via Enchantress. You play [[Mesmerism]] on it. Even after it returns to being a normal aura, you would normally control it, but I control it while King Arthur is in the realm.

title: FAQ: King of the Realm
text:
Q: What Mortals are affected by the first ability?
A: All Mortals, anywhere in the realm.

title: FAQ: Kingdom of Agartha
text:
Q: If Kingdom of Agartha's ability is active, can I choose to summon minions underground without a printed Burrowing ability?
A: Yes. Kingdom of Agartha affects minions everywhere.

title: FAQ: Kythera Mechanism
text:
Q: How does this interact with Court Jester?
A: You don't get to look at your opponent's hand, but you do get to choose which of their cards they discard (e.g. site or spell).

title: FAQ: Lacuna Entity
text:
Q: What happens if the power of one of the units changes during the resolution of this effect so that it's no longer weaker?
A: Only check that the target is weaker when it is initially targeted, and when the effect first starts to resolve from the storyline. Once the effect is resolving and minions are moving, it does not matter if the relative powers change after that point.

title: FAQ: Land Deed
text:
Q: What happens if I have a minion that occupies more than one site (e.g. Mountain Giant) and also carries Land Deed?
A: Land Deed only grants you control of the site that Land Deed occupies.

title: FAQ: Lava Salamander
text:
Q: What counts as a 'fire spell'?
A: Once a minion, aura, or artifact enters the realm, it is no longer considered a 'spell.' Magic never enters the realm, so it is still considered a spell while it is resolving. In effect, Lava Salamander is immune to fire Magic.

title: FAQ: Leap Attack
text:
Q: Does this card count as an 'attack' since it has the word 'attack' in its name?
A: Sorry for the confusion, but no, this is not actually an attack! You only get an 'attack' from the Move and Attack basic ability, or card text that specifically uses the word attack (e.g. Crave Golem). This card text uses the word 'strike,' which means the unit simply deals damage equal to its power (and there's no chance for the opponent to Defend, and you can strike Stealthed or Airborne units, etc.)

title: FAQ: Legion of Gall
text:
Q: What if there are fewer than three cards in the chosen collection?
A: You banish all of the remaining cards.

title: FAQ: Lightning Bolt
text:
Q: Can I lightning bolt the void?
A: Yes, but only if the spellcaster is in the void (since Lightning Bolt targets, the spellcaster must be in the same region).

title: FAQ: Lilith
text:
Q: What happens if Lilith summons a minion with an end of turn ability (e.g. Infernal Legion)?
A: Their ability will not trigger this turn.

title: FAQ: Locusts of Illyria
text:
Q: Do I summon a copy the turn I first summon the Locusts?
A: Yes! At the end of the turn you first summon them, they will see that there are no 'new' Locusts (meaning Locusts summoned by the triggered ability), and thus summon a copy. The following turn if you still have two in the realm, you'll only get one more.

title: FAQ: Lord of Fear
text:
Q: What does 'defend alone' mean?
A: When the Defend window closes (see '((Attack))' in the codex for details), If only a single enemy unit uses the Defend ability, the Defender is removed from the fight and the original attack target is reinstated. Defenders still arrive one at a time, but if there's only one, the defense effectively is negated (though that one defender still got to tap and move to the attack's location).

title: FAQ: Lord of Greed
text:
Q: How do I properly resolve this effect?
A: Lord of Greed may and must take a carriable artifact from anywhere in the realm, including from another unit sharing a location with him. In this case, 'elsewhere' means anywhere other than Lord of Greed's hands! He will take from allies as well. This does not target the artifact, so even artifacts carried by minions with stealth are not safe from Lord of Greed.

title: FAQ: Lucky Charm
text:
Q: The alpha and beta text is different, which should I use?
A: The beta text is correct.

title: FAQ: Lure
text:
Q: Can my allied minion tempt an enemy in a different region to take a step closer?
A: Yes, as long as they occupy a nearby site, they can be above or below that site.  However, they cannot be tempted to take a step into a region they couldn't normally move into (e.g. they cannot be made to step underground if they do not have Burrowing).

title: FAQ: Maddening Bells
text:
Q: If Maddening Bells tries to increase the cost of a spell that has an alternate casting cost of zero (e.g. Deathspeaker ability while on death's door, Aramos Mercenaries), what happens?
A: The spell costs zero. See '((Cost))' for more details.

title: FAQ: Maelström
text:
Q: Does the movement get resolved simultaneously?
A: Yes, all the steps are simultaneously resolved (which might then provoke a variety of triggers).

title: FAQ: Magellan Globe
text:
Q: If Magellan Globe is in play, can an aura or an oversized unit be cast on the edge of the realm, spanning the realm?
A: Yes. Ensure that the game state is clear, so all players know which sites the aura occupies, using notes as needed.

title: FAQ: Magician
text:
Q: What if an effect directs me to draw a spell, but it turns out there's a site on top of my spellbook?
A: All cards in your spellbook are considered spells while in your spellbook, so you can draw it normally.

title: FAQ: Makeshift Barricade
text:
Q: If I do 1 damage to three minions simultaneously, does the Barricade break?
A: Yes, because 1+1+1 = 3 damage dealt all at the same time.

title: FAQ: Mariner's Curse
text:
Q: What if this is animated by an Enchantress?
A: If an animated Mariner's Curse moves and enters a water site, it will submerge itself (if possible) and die (assuming it doesn't have Submerge). If it hasn't died, it will then return itself to its owner's hand. It will not have a chance to attack before its effect resolves, because the move happens before the attack.

title: FAQ: Mask of Mayhem
text:
Q: If I double twice, is it multiplied by 4?
A: Yes.

title: FAQ: Master Tracker
text:
Q: What does it mean to 'permanently lose stealth'?
A: Simply remove the stealth token. It does not prevent the minion from gaining stealth later.

title: FAQ: Mayor of Milborne
text:
Q: Does this buff my opponent's Mortals as well?
A: Yes! The Mayor wants as many votes as possible!

title: FAQ: Megalurker
text:
Q: Can this Genesis effect drag a minion into a different region?
A: Yes, due to the golden rule. Because avatars cannot enter non-surface locations, if one is being dragged by this effect they will be dragged as far as they can while staying within the surface region.

title: FAQ: Megamoeba
text:
Q: If I play Dodge Roll on my Megamoeba, does the attack still go through because the Megamoeba is still occupying the original location?
A: Yes, the target is still valid, but Megamoeba now has +1 power from the extra location it occupies thanks to Dodge Roll.

title: FAQ: Mephistopheles
text:
Q: How do I resolve this effect?
A: If you cast Mephistopheles, your Avatar is banished. Mephistopheles is now your Avatar. He retains Unique rarity, Demon type, and Air element, but he's no longer a minion and only an Avatar. Your current and maximum life remain the same. Notably, you won't be able to play sites normally because Mephistopheles doesn't have that ability. You will still be able to cast spells because Avatars are spellcasters as one of their characteristics. If you manage to summon Mephistopheles without casting him, then he will not replace your avatar, but his second ability will still function.

title: FAQ: Merlin
text:
Q: How does Merlin's ability work and what does 'any time' actually permit?
A: This is a passive ability, usable any time on your turn, including during your start phase before you draw a card. But, you may still only cast spells when they are normally permitted to be cast (i.e. during your Main Phase when nothing else is on the storyline other than this ability). Technically, if a Crave Golem were attacking during your Start Phase, Merlin could cast a Dodge Roll then!

title: FAQ: Meteor Shower
text:
Q: Can I choose sites that share a corner?
A: Yes. 'Border' means adjacent squares, not including diagonals.

title: FAQ: Mimic
text:
Q: How does this ability work?
A: When you summon Mimic, you can choose to summon it normally, or instead you can choose a carriable artifact anywhere in the realm. That artifact is banished, and the Mimic is placed at the artifact's location instead as it transforms.  You control the Mimic, and if the artifact did not enter the realm this turn, the Mimic doesn't have Summoning Sickness. It turns out that artifact was a Mimic in disguise all along!

title: FAQ: Miracle Workers
text:
Q: If multiple minions including Miracle Workers die at the same time on Geistwood, can Miracle Workers return themselves and/or another minion that's dying to your hand?
A: No, because Miracle Workers only return minions from the cemetery, and deathrites resolve while the minions are still in the realm. The Miracle Workers could return other minions that died earlier that turn and were in the cemetery.

title: FAQ: Mirage
text:
Q: What happens if I try to use Mirage's alternate play text when it's played via Pathfinder?
A: When using the Pathfinder's ability, you reveal the site, then play it in an adjacent Rubble or void (then Pathfinder moves there). Mirage's ability cannot be combined with Pathfinder.

title: FAQ: Mirror Realm
text:
Q: How do Smokestacks of Gnaak and Mirror Realm interact?
A: By the time Mirror ))Realm(( enters the realm, it's already a copy. Thus, it can copy a nearby site, and then promptly loses all abilities of that copied site (but still is the copy, without abilities). See '((Apply Ongoing Effects In Order))' in the codex for nitty-gritty details.

title: FAQ: Mismanaged Mortuary
text:
Q: Once this is in play, do I put cards into the cemetery that I own or the cemetery that I control?
A: You always put your cards into the cemetery you own (the one nearby your deck).

title: FAQ: Monstermorphosis
text:
Q: If I transform an enemy minion into a Monster from my hand or Horrible Hybrids from my collection, who controls it?
A: The controller of the minion does not change when transforming, so in that case your opponent would control it. Note cards always go to their owner's cemetery so when that minion dies it will go to your cemetery.

title: FAQ: Moonsong Talagelum
text:
Q: Since this 'counts as Grey Wolves' does that mean I can include any number of it in my spellbook?
A: No. The phrase 'counts as Grey Wolves' means that other cards will see it as being named 'Grey Wolves' in addition to its normal name. You still must follow rarity restrictions.

title: FAQ: Morgana le Fay
text:
Q: Where do I keep Morgana's hand of cards?
A: See '((Only It Can Cast))' in the codex.

title: FAQ: Mother Nature
text:
Q: Does 'here' mean Mother Nature's location or site?
A: 'Here' references Mother Nature's exact location.

title: FAQ: Mount Ussar Sanctuary
text:
Q: When I flee, is it step by step movement or teleportation?
A: It's step by step movement!

title: FAQ: Mountain Giant
text:
Q: What happens if a Mountain Giant occupies a Silence aura?
A: A card's size is generally set when it enters the realm, and is considered one of its characteristics, not an ability. It will not resize.

title: FAQ: Mountain Pass
text:
Q: You have a minion on my Mountain Pass. Can I summon a minion on the site?
A: Yes. Though summoning is included in 'entering,' it is not moving on the ground. So you can summon all you want, since summoning isn't moving.

title: FAQ: Mudflow
text:
Q: Once I target the site, do I also pick 'surface' or 'unburrow?'
A: No, you simply target the site, and then the proper action is applied. If a water site is the target, minions there are surfaced. If a land site is the target, minions there are unburrowed.

title: FAQ: Mudslide
text:
Q: Do I pick left or right for all units together, or can I choose different directions?
A: Choose left or right, and apply it to every unit at land sites in the column.

title: FAQ: Occult Ritual
text:
Q: The alpha, alternate art version of this card from the pledge pack has the text 'Spellcaster nearby,' while the regular foil and non-foil versions have the text 'Spellcaster here.' which is correct?
A: The normal version is correct. The text should be 'Spellcaster here.' The alternate art version is not legal for tournament play.

title: FAQ: Old Salt Anchorman
text:
Q: Does this ability protect my minions from movement effects like forceful burrowing (e.g. Bury), submerge (e.g. Drown), and teleportation (e.g. Chaos Twister)?
A: Yes, all of those effects are movement. With Chaos Twister, don't even attempt to blow the card if the target is an ally nearby Old Salt Anchorman.

title: FAQ: Onslaught
text:
Q: How does this Magic work?
A: Onslaught creates an ongoing effect which lasts the duration of your turn and continually prevents your units from being immobilized, silenced, or disabled. A minion cast after Onslaught resolves would be protected, and would gain +1 power and Charge. Note that Onslaught does not remove any ongoing effects which may be disabling, silencing or immobilizing your units, it just suppresses them for the duration of your turn.  For example, if you play Onslaught and then summon a [[Slumbering Giantess]], her Genesis ability will still resolve, and she will be disabled when the effect of Onslaught wears off. For the duration of your turn, however, she will have +1 power and Charge, and will ignore the disable effect from her Genesis ability.

title: FAQ: Onyx Core
text:
Q: When does this artifact provide mana?
A: When it enters the realm, and at the start of its controller's turn.

title: FAQ: Orb of Ba'al Berith
text:
Q: Is the Orb the spellcaster for the copied spell?
A: Yes.

title: FAQ: Order of the White Wing
text:
Q: Does the minion that's being summoned from elsewhere enter the realm for a moment before it's banished?
A: No, it doesn't ever enter the realm. For example, it will not trigger a Genesis, it will not get a Lance, it will not trigger a Mariner's Curse, etc. It doesn't actually enter the realm at all, since this is a replacement effect.

title: FAQ: Ormund Harpooneers
text:
Q: Does the target need to be in the same region as the Harpooneers?
A: No. Normally the answer is yes, but the card text 'above or ((below))' means that normal targeting restrictions are ignored, and the Harpooneers can be in any region (surface, underground, underwater, or in the void). As long as there is an adjacent Water site to the Harpooneers and a minion occupying that water site, it will get pulled to the Harpooneers' location.

title: FAQ: Orpheus' Crossing
text:
Q: On my turn when I go to Death's Door, can I still take damage and lose life?
A: Yes. You cannot lose the game due to taking damage, but taking damage and losing life will reduce your life total if possible. See '((Death's Door))' for more details.

title: FAQ: Pact with the Devil
text:
Q: If a non-minion (e.g. River of Flame, or Orb of Ba'al Berith) is the spellcaster, can I sacrifice it?
A: Yes!

title: FAQ: Panpipes of Pnom
text:
Q: Does this cause a zero power unit to deal 2 damage when striking?
A: Yes, this effect will cause zero power units to strike for 2 damage.

title: FAQ: Pathfinder
text:
Q: The alpha and beta text is different, which should I use?
A: The beta text is correct.

title: FAQ: Payload Trebuchet
text:
Q: Do both units need to have been in play for a turn or have charge?
A: Yes. Summoning sick units can't be tapped to pay costs.

title: FAQ: Peace Offering
text:
Q: What does 'can't attack you' actually mean?
A: The other player can't attack anything you control (units or sites).

title: FAQ: Perilous Bridge
text:
Q: Can a unit be moved through the top border of this site by force?
A: No, assuming the unit does not have the Airborne ability.  Effects which drag/push/pull a unit cannot cause it to move through the top border of this site while on the ground.  For instance, a non-Airborne minion cannot use  [[Grapple Shot]] to pass through this border, and a [[Pudge Butcher]] cannot pull a non-Airborne unit through it. Teleport effects do not pass through borders, however, and are not considered movement on the ground, so they can allow a unit to ))move(( to a location on the other side.

title: FAQ: Persecutor
text:
Q: Can I brand an enemy and step toward the closest Evil on the same turn?
A: No, you must choose only one option each turn.

title: FAQ: Phantom Steed
text:
Q: What happens when a minion carries another minion that's carrying a minion?
A: Only the minions you're directly carrying count against your limit. Have fun at the carnival!

title: FAQ: Philosopher's Stone
text:
Q: How does the Philosopher's Stone work with multi-element cards, such as King Arthur and Queen Guienevere? Would King Arthur, who requires 4 mana, cost 3 or 0 Mana to cast using the Stone?
A: Cards that have different element symbols count as a spell of each of those affinities. So Arthur and Guinevere are each an Air spell, an Earth spell, a Fire spell, and a Water spell, all at the same time. But you are still casting them together as a single spell. So, assuming Arthur is your spellcaster's first spell of the turn, the Stone will offer a discount of 1 mana for Arthur, making him cost 3 mana. 

This also means that when Arthur is played he uses up the Stone for that spellcaster's turn because he's simultaneously the first Air, Earth, Fire, and Water spell played this turn. So the Spellcaster cannot continue to use the stone that turn.

title: FAQ: Pied Piper of Hameln
text:
Q: What happens if a second Pied Piper of Hameln enters play?
A: You apply each of their abilities in timestamp order. The first Piper takes control of all minions with 1 or less power, then the second Piper will take control of them. The controller of the second Piper will end up controlling all minions with 1 or less power.

title: FAQ: Pilgrim's Shrine
text:
Q: What happens if the minion which leaves this site can't be warded (e.g. it has a Ward already or it's Evil)?
A: The Ward remains on the site, as it cannot be transferred.

title: FAQ: Pillar of Zeiros
text:
Q: How does this interact with effects which modify healing (e.g. River of Blood)?
A: You banish all dead minions, count them, and then heal once for a total amount equal to the number of dead minions which were banished. [[River of Blood]] would halve, rounding down, that final total.

title: FAQ: Pith Imp
text:
Q: Where does the stolen spell go?
A: It goes to a separate zone as if the Pith Imp was carrying the spell; it does not go to your hand. You may look at the spell and your opponent may not (though they do get to see the spell at the moment you steal it).

title: FAQ: Plague of Frogs
text:
Q: Where can I summon the frogs?
A: You can summon each of them to whatever locations will cause maximum annoyance.

title: FAQ: Polar Explorers
text:
Q: If Polar Explorers or Ruler of Thul are in play and an oversized unit on the top row moves 'up' one row to wrap around to the bottom, what happens?
A: This ability only allows movement across the borders, not ongoing occupation. Units cannot balance on the edge of the realm and an oversized unit that finds its way there falls to one side or the other. Its controller places it in the closest legal position, controller's choice if tied.

title: FAQ: Pollimorph
text:
Q: Does a pollimorphed animated aura (e.g. Enchantress) return to an aura form later?
A: No. It is permanently a Frog token, and occupies a single location.

title: FAQ: Pristine Paradise
text:
Q: Does Pristine Paradise provide mana the turn the Pathfinder plays it from the atlas? That is, does the site have enough time to make mana before the Pathfinder moves onto it?
A: Yes, sites immediately generate mana when they come into play.

title: FAQ: Quagmire
text:
Q: If the genesis resolves, and then my opponent plays Smokestacks of Gnaak nearby, does the Quagmire effect continue?
A: Yes. The genesis ability creates an effect that lasts until the start of your next turn.

title: FAQ: Queen Guinevere
text:
Q: How does the Philosopher's Stone work with multi-element cards, such as King Arthur and Queen Guienevere? Would King Arthur, who requires 4 mana, cost 3 or 0 Mana to cast using the Stone?
A: Cards that have different element symbols count as a spell of each of those affinities. So Arthur and Guinevere are each an Air spell, an Earth spell, a Fire spell, and a Water spell, all at the same time. But you are still casting them together as a single spell. So, assuming Arthur is your spellcaster's first spell of the turn, the Stone will offer a discount of 1 mana for Arthur, making him cost 3 mana. 

This also means that when Arthur is played he uses up the Stone for that spellcaster's turn because he's simultaneously the first Air, Earth, Fire, and Water spell played this turn. So the Spellcaster cannot continue to use the stone that turn.

title: FAQ: Questing Beast
text:
Q: Does this end of turn ability cause the Beast to lose stealth?
A: No, as it is a triggered ability it does not cause the Beast to interact with the realm.

title: FAQ: Raise Dead
text:
Q: Where can I summon the raised minion?
A: After randomly determining the dead minion, you may summon it anywhere.

title: FAQ: Raze
text:
Q: Does this destroy artifacts underneath the site, or just ones on the surface?
A: Artifacts both above and below the site are destroyed.

title: FAQ: Realm-Eater
text:
Q: How does this ability work?
A: Whenever ))Realm-Eater(( attacks a site and strikes it, that site is destroyed and the ))Realm-Eater(( gains an ongoing effect causing it to be immobile. You can activate ))Realm-Eater's(( digest ability to remove one instance of this immobilizing effect, but if you have attacked and destroyed multiple sites you must digest each one.

title: FAQ: Red Rock of Ravannis
text:
Q: What does 'Artifacts can't be carried here' mean?
A: Artifacts which share a location with the Red Rock are no longer carried. They are not dropped, they just stop being carried, so the effect will still apply to artifacts which cannot be dropped. These artifacts also cannot be targeted by the Pick Up ability.

title: FAQ: Redmane Hyena
text:
Q: Does the Hyena stop being a Beast if it becomes a Demon?
A: No, it will be both a Demon and a Beast.

title: FAQ: Regurgitator
text:
Q: How does this ability work?
A: If the Regurgitator has an empty belly and there are any dead minions, you must fill its belly by banishing one. If it has a full belly, you must empty it by shooting a projectile. If it has an empty belly and there are no dead minions, nothing happens.

title: FAQ: Release the Hounds
text:
Q: Can I play this with only one Hellhound in my collection?
A: Yes. You will only summon that one [[Hellhound]].

title: FAQ: Replication
text:
Q: Where can I conjure the copy?
A: You can conjure it anywhere.

title: FAQ: Rhongomyniad
text:
Q: How does this work?
A: After the throw, Rhongomyniad is in the final location along its path, and is not carried by any unit.

title: FAQ: Riddle Sphinx
text:
Q: Can I draw a site with this effect?
A: Try this riddle: Which spell will I draw? Fooled you! Neither of them! (Yes, you can draw a site.)

title: FAQ: Rift Valley
text:
Q: Can you 'pull apart' a row with a single site?
A: No. That's not what 'pull apart' means.

title: FAQ: Ring of Morrigan
text:
Q: If the damage from this trigger is prevented or redirected, do I still gain 1 life?
A: No, you must deal at least 1 point of damage with the ability to gain any life.

title: FAQ: Riptide
text:
Q: Can riptide pull a voidwalk minion in the void?
A: No, because minions in the void aren't 'aboveground.'

title: FAQ: River of Blood
text:
Q: If there are two Rivers of Blood in play, do they stack?
A: Yes. Half the healing (rounding down), then half the healing again (round down). So [[Divine Healing]] would heal 1 with two Rivers of Blood in play.

title: FAQ: River of Flame
text:
Q: If River of Flame casts a spell, choosing the surface, but there are Maddening Bells underground, is the River of Flame affected?
A: Yes! Those bells are so loud (and still nearby the caster).

title: FAQ: River Rapids
text:
Q: What is a 'connected river'?
A: Connected rivers are a contiguous group of adjacent sites with River in their name, regardless of who controls them, and which contains River Rapids. River Rapids is, by definition, connected to itself, even if it is not connected to any other Rivers.

title: FAQ: Roaming Monster
text:
Q: The term 'summon' means 'enter the realm.' So, does that mean I can play this minion for free?
A: No. This effect simply provides additional locations where you may summon this minion.

title: FAQ: Rolling Boulder
text:
Q: What happens if Magellan Globe is in play and I push it along a complete row or column?
A: The Rolling Boulder continues until it would repeat a step (i.e. back to where it started), and then stops instead of repeating a step. It doesn't do 8 damage on the starting location, since a location is either along its path or not.

title: FAQ: Roots of Yggdrasil
text:
Q: What happens to destroyed Rubble?
A: Nothing (it turns into more Rubble, and thus doesn't change).

title: FAQ: Rowdy Boys
text:
Q: When exactly is 'after striking' ?
A: After effects concurrent with striking (e.g. after gaining life via Daperyll Vampire), but before any Deathrite abilities resolve. It's in the same moment that Stealth would break due to striking.

title: FAQ: Ruby Core
text:
Q: When does this artifact provide mana?
A: When it enters the realm, and at the start of its controller's turn.

title: FAQ: Ruler of Thul
text:
Q: If Polar Explorers or Ruler of Thul are in play and an oversized unit on the top row moves 'up' one row to wrap around to the bottom, what happens?
A: This ability only allows movement across the borders, not ongoing occupation. Units cannot balance on the edge of the realm and an oversized unit that finds its way there falls to one side or the other. Its controller places it in the closest legal position, controller's choice if tied.

title: FAQ: Saint of Redemption
text:
Q: Does 'no minion is Evil' mean they are no longer considered a Demon, Monster or Undead?
A: Minions will still keep their Demon, Monster and Undead types! They simply are no longer Evil, and will not be affected by things which specifically affect Evil.

title: FAQ: Scatter
text:
Q: Can I push an oversized unit?
A: Yes, choose a cardinal direction and push the oversized unit one step in that direction as long as no part of the unit would change regions.

title: FAQ: Scent Hounds
text:
Q: What does it mean to 'permanently lose stealth'?
A: Simply remove the stealth token. It does not prevent the minion from gaining stealth later.

title: FAQ: Scorched Earth
text:
Q: A minion with Gilded Aegis is on a site chosen for Scorched Earth. The Aegis and the minion are being destroyed simultaneously. Does the Aegis have a chance to save the minion before it's destroyed?
A: Yes.

title: FAQ: Scourge Zombies
text:
Q: If Scourge Zombies and an allied mortal die at the same time (e.g. Minor Explosion), does the Zombie's ability bring it back immediately?
A: No, since the Scourge Zombies must be in the cemetery for their ability to trigger when the mortal dies.

title: FAQ: Screamer
text:
Q: Who decides where the minion steps?
A: The controller of Screamer.

title: FAQ: Sea Raider
text:
Q: If Sea Raider attacks a 3 power minion, killing it but also dying in the process, does the Raider have time to use their ability before they die?
A: Yes. After units are killed, there is time for effects to resolve (e.g. Deathrite) before minions are placed in cemeteries. This effect resolves in the same window of time as deathrites.

title: FAQ: Searing Truth
text:
Q: Does this actually target the Avatar?
A: Yes. If your opponent casts this and targets your Warded avatar, you will not draw any cards and the Ward will break. Normal targeting rules apply (e.g. a spellcaster in the void or subsurface couldn't target an avatar with this magic, since they aren't in the same region).

title: FAQ: Seasoned Sellsword
text:
Q: If my avatar is nearby Seasoned Sellsword, can I discard a card for her ability even if I already control her?
A: Yes!

title: FAQ: Seirawan Hydra
text:
Q: How can I kill a Hydra?
A: Deal 1 lethal damage, or 6 damage all at once. Multiple sources of simultaneous damage will work. For example, if the Hydra attacks and two [[Bosk Troll]]s defend, the Hydra will be killed. Note that damage done one at a time, e.g. [[Arcane Barrage]], would not kill it, since each individual 1 damage would be immediately healed.

title: FAQ: Selfsame Simulacrum
text:
Q: If it tries to become a basic copy of an aura animated by Enchantress, what happens?
A: Selfsame Simulacrum becomes an aura (not a minion), since that's the actual text on the animated aura. As soon as Selfsame Simulacrum is an aura, it expands to its proper size based on card text (and default aura rules), and must continue to occupy the location that was specified during casting.

title: FAQ: Sentinel Trap
text:
Q: How is the facing for the Trap determined?
A: When you conjure the Sentinel Trap into the realm, choose a cardinal direction to be its initial facing. It then rotates from there. If it is teleported, the controller of the teleport effect can choose which cardinal direction it ends up facing.

title: FAQ: Shackled Demon
text:
Q: Does the Spellcaster have to be a unit to tap and release the Demon?
A: Yes.  Only units can tap, so a spellcaster artifact or site would be unable to release the demon.

title: FAQ: Shield Maidens
text:
Q: My Shield Maidens attack, and then 3 Foot Soldiers defend. How much damage do my Shield Maidens take?
A: 0, because each source of damage is reduced by 1!

title: FAQ: Shrike Orchard
text:
Q: Can this target sub-surface minions?
A: Yes.  The minion must be nearby to the site, which means it must be near one of the site's locations.  This means that minions which are underground (or underwater, if the Shrike Orchard is flooded) can be targeted by this effect.

title: FAQ: Siege Ballista
text:
Q: Do both units need to have been in play for a turn or have charge?
A: Yes. Summoning sick units can't be tapped to pay costs.

title: FAQ: Silence
text:
Q: What happens if a Mountain Giant occupies a Silence aura?
A: A card's size is generally set when it enters the realm, and is considered one of its characteristics, not an ability. It will not resize.

title: FAQ: Silver Bullet
text:
Q: Can the bearer cast the spell, even if they're not a spellcaster?
A: Yes!

title: FAQ: Sinister Pond
text:
Q: How do I calculate the difference in cost of the two minions?
A: Start with the cost of the Evil minion in your hand, then subtract the cost of the Mortal at the Pond. Remember that costs cannot be negative, so if the result is below zero, treat it as zero instead.

title: FAQ: Sir Morien
text:
Q: Can enemy projectiles be shot from Morien's location?
A: No, Morien cuts them down immediately, like the total badass he is.

title: FAQ: Sir Tom Thumb
text:
Q: If my opponent's beast snatches Tom up, do they now take control of him?
A: How dare you!? Sir Tom Thumb is no mere trinket. He's a fully autonomous being and acknowledges no other controller!

title: FAQ: Skeleton Mage
text:
Q: If Deathspeaker uses his ability to cast Skeleton Mage, does the Skeleton Mage get to use its genesis ability (casting and resolving a spell) before being banished?
A: Yes!

title: FAQ: Skirmishers of Mu
text:
Q: How does this ability work?
A: After declaring their movement path but before actually moving, Skirmishers may shoot. (The game will lookahead to see if your declared path will actually result in movement, ignoring all triggered abilities but considering all ongoing effects.) Alternately, Skirmishers may shoot when they enter a new location during basic movement. They get one shot total during their basic movement, regardless of how far they move. Note that basic movement includes movement from a basic ability, i.e. Move and Attack, and Defend.

title: FAQ: Slimy Mutants
text:
Q: Is this an activated ability that I use while Slimy Mutants are in my hand?
A: Yes! While Slimy Mutants are in your hand, you may pay (3) and resolve the effect.

title: FAQ: Slumbering Giantess
text:
Q: If attacked by a minion that strikes first, does the Giantess end up striking back?
A: Yes, assuming she isn't killed.

title: FAQ: Smokestacks of Gnaak
text:
Q: What happens if there are two Smokestacks of Gnaak nearby each other?
A: See '((Example - Two Smokestacks of Gnaak))' in the codex!

title: FAQ: Snowball
text:
Q: Are minions along the path affected even if they have stealth?
A: Yes! Projectiles do not hit stealth minions, but Snowball is just using the projectile to draw a path. It doesn't matter what units are hit, all of them along the path are rolled up in the snowball and pulled along!

title: FAQ: Sow the Earth
text:
Q: If I happen to play a Lone Tower from the top of my atlas, will the mana from the Genesis ability also be doubled? What about mana from Abundance?
A: Yes. Any mana that the site produces, including via any abilities, will be doubled.

title: FAQ: Sparkmage
text:
Q: Can any of my spellcasters cast a spell and still benefit from my avatar's ability?
A: Yes! As long as you control the spellcaster, the game sees it as a spell '((you))' cast, meaning the player.

title: FAQ: Spear of Destiny
text:
Q: What if the minion being killed occupies more than one location?
A: You choose where the spear teleports, which will be a single location the minion occupies.

title: FAQ: Sphere of Animosity
text:
Q: What does 'Avatars here can't leave' mean?
A: Avatars currently under the Sphere of Animosity can't enter locations not occupied by the Sphere. This means they can't move to those locations, or be moved by force. Note that when a site moves, it carries along cards of normal size with it, and those cards do not count as entering a new location. This means that a moving site can carry an Avatar out of the Sphere.

title: FAQ: Spin Attack
text:
Q: Does this card count as an 'attack' since it has the word 'attack' in its name?
A: Sorry for the confusion, but no, this is not actually an attack! You only get an 'attack' from the Move and Attack basic ability, or card text that specifically uses the word attack (e.g. Crave Golem). This card text uses the word 'strike,' which means the unit simply deals damage equal to its power (and there's no chance for the opponent to Defend, and you can strike Stealthed or Airborne units, etc.)

title: FAQ: Spire Lich
text:
Q: Does Spire satisfy the Spire Lich?
A: Yes, because of the golden rule. Be cool!

title: FAQ: Spore Spouts
text:
Q: When is the power of the minion checked to see if it's small enough to summon to any site?
A: You check at the time of casting, before the minion enters the realm. This means that you can summon a Vengeful Heir to any site, even if it enters the realm as a minion which would be too large to work with Spore Sprouts normally, for example.

title: FAQ: Squirming Mass
text:
Q: Let's say the Mass is 1 power, and it fights another 1 power minion. What happens?
A: Both take 1 damage each, which results in their simultaneous death. That triggers Squirming Mass's ability, which means its gains +1 power, but it's already dying, and merely gaining power isn't enough to save it. (Something specifically that saves a unit from death would be necessary, like Gilded Aegis.) In this example, both minions are placed in the cemetery.

title: FAQ: Stagecoach
text:
Q: Can this Pick Up and carry enemy minions?
A: Yes, the coach will carry anyone!

title: FAQ: Stitched Abomination
text:
Q: How does this ability work?
A: The Abomination takes damage as if it is one unit, but the player causing the damage can choose which part or parts of the Abomination it applies to (after damage reduction, if any). Once a part has enough damage assigned to kill it, it's removed. When the last part of the Abomination is destroyed, so is the Abomination. For example, I have an Abomination with 5 + 4 + 3 power, and you are dealing it 7 damage from a Major Explosion. You can assign 3 and 4 damage, destroying those parts, and it's left with 5 power. Alternately, if it were my own Major Explosion, I could assign 3 damage to the 5-power part, and 3 damage to the 4-power part, and 1 damage to 3-power part. It's left with 5+4+3 power, with some damage on each of those parts (which will be removed normally at end of turn).  If an effect would destroy or kill the Abomination outright, including taking Lethal damage, all of its parts are killed. If an effect would banish the Abomination, all of it is banished.

title: FAQ: Sturmgeist
text:
Q: When does this ability resolve?
A: Whenever an enemy announces a Magic spell, after they've paid the costs but before the spell resolves.

title: FAQ: Summoning Sphere
text:
Q: Does this allow me to summon my units burrowed even without burrowing?
A: No. The effect only allows you to break the restriction of choosing one of your own sites, but not the rule about summoning atop the site.

title: FAQ: Sunken Treasure
text:
Q: Do I get the cards immediately when my minion carrying the treasure moves to the surface, even in the middle of something else (like defending or attacking) ?
A: Yes! As soon as your unit is on the surface, you resolve the treasure effect.

title: FAQ: Swap
text:
Q: If one target is a minion, can the other target be an artifact, and vice versa?
A: Yes. Target one (minion or artifact) and target another (minion or artifact).

title: FAQ: Symmetric Suffering
text:
Q: How do I resolve this effect if I sacrifice a card that has multiple types (e.g. Automaton) ?
A: When you sacrifice a card that has multiple types, you may specify which type your opponent must match. For example, if you sacrifice one automaton (Minion and Artifact), you can force your opponent to sacrifice a minion or an artifact, your choice (not both). Similarly, if you're playing as Enchantress and you sacrifice an animated aura (Minion and Aura), you can force your opponent to sacrifice a minion or an aura, your choice (not both).

title: FAQ: Tactical Move
text:
Q: What is the timing for the resolution of this spell?
A: Choose an ally, declare its movement steps, placing them on the Storyline, then resolve those steps. Repeat for each ally. That is, you declare and resolve each ally's steps before proceeding to the next ally. If you gain more allies during the resolution, you may move them too; keep repeating the effect until each ally has moved.

title: FAQ: Templar
text:
Q: Can any of my spellcasters cast a spell and still benefit from my avatar's ability?
A: Yes! As long as you control the spellcaster, the game sees it as a spell '((you))' cast, meaning the player.

title: FAQ: Thankless Squire
text:
Q: Once the Thankless Squire has delivered all those lances, and isn't carrying any more, is it still Immobile?
A: Yes, he's very tired and in need of a rest.

title: FAQ: The Apex of Babel
text:
Q: What does it mean to 'build The Tower of Babel' and 'play ... atop this' ?
A: You may play The Apex of Babel onto the same square as The Base of Babel! (If you have multiple copes of The Base of Babel in the realm, choose one.) If you do, they merge into a single site called The Tower of Babel. When you build it by playing the Apex, resolve the effect on The Apex of Babel. The Tower of Babel is considered a single site that provides (2) mana and (A)(E), and is both Unique and Exceptional. (The turn you play it, you gain (1) more mana since the Base was already in play.) If it's destroyed, both The Apex of Babel and The Base of Babel go to your cemetery. If it's copied, e.g. Mirror Realm, the copy will provide (2) mana, etc., but you won't get the build bonus again. For all purposes, The Tower of Babel is considered a single site.

title: FAQ: The Base of Babel
text:
Q: What does it mean to 'build The Tower of Babel' and 'play ... atop this' ?
A: You may play The Apex of Babel onto the same square as The Base of Babel! (If you have multiple copes of The Base of Babel in the realm, choose one.) If you do, they merge into a single site called The Tower of Babel. When you build it by playing the Apex, resolve the effect on The Apex of Babel. The Tower of Babel is considered a single site that provides (2) mana and (A)(E), and is both Unique and Exceptional. (The turn you play it, you gain (1) more mana since the Base was already in play.) If it's destroyed, both The Apex of Babel and The Base of Babel go to your cemetery. If it's copied, e.g. Mirror Realm, the copy will provide (2) mana, etc., but you won't get the build bonus again. For all purposes, The Tower of Babel is considered a single site.

title: FAQ: The Colour Out of Space
text:
Q: If it's not adjacent to void and is within Abundance, does it still gain extra mana?
A: Yes. The site doesn't provide mana normally, but if it's modified in some way (e.g. Abundance), then it can provide additional mana. 0 + 1 = 1.

title: FAQ: The Doom of Dilmun
text:
Q: Can this minion die?
A: The only way it can be killed is if you sacrifice it. Otherwise, it cannot be killed. Meet your doom!

title: FAQ: The Flood
text:
Q: If Draconian Bonekite, Sir Pelleas, and Azuridge Caravan are all in the realm, can I choose to keep the Caravan and another minion?
A: No, you cannot save Azuridge Caravan and other minions. Since Azuridge Caravan counts as all minion types, you cannot save it and any other minion with a type since they will always have a shared type.

title: FAQ: The Geistwood
text:
Q: If multiple minions including Miracle Workers die at the same time on Geistwood, can Miracle Workers return themselves and/or another minion that's dying to your hand?
A: No, because Miracle Workers only return minions from the cemetery, and deathrites resolve while the minions are still in the realm. The Miracle Workers could return other minions that died earlier that turn and were in the cemetery.

title: FAQ: The Hexham Haunts
text:
Q: How does summoning burrowed interact with Evil Presence?
A: You may summon the Haunts to an affected site, and they must be burrowed. But the Haunts won't gain Charge and Evil Presence will remain in the realm because the Haunts were not summoned 'here' according to Evil Presence, since Evil Presence occupies the surface (and perhaps the void), not underground.

title: FAQ: The Immortal Throne
text:
Q: What does 'alone here' mean?
A: No other units at the location.

title: FAQ: The Inquisition
text:
Q: When does this ability trigger?
A: If an effect requires you to reveal it from your hand, or from your spellbook, or if your opponent searches your spellbook.

title: FAQ: The Malleus Maleficarum
text:
Q: Can the bearer cast the spell, even if they're not a spellcaster?
A: Yes!

title: FAQ: The Manor at Daperyll Hill
text:
Q: If the 3 damage is reduced, redirected away from 'here', or prevented, do I still heal 3?
A: No, the full 3 damage must be dealt to the targeted minion here in order to heal 3.

title: FAQ: The Rack
text:
Q: Stretch my avatar? You're pulling my leg! Does this make my avatar an oversized unit now?
A: Pulling both arms and both legs actually but, yes! Your avatar will now be an oversized unit!

title: FAQ: The Void
text:
Q: How does this site work?
A: The site still has both a surface and subsurface, but those locations also count as void simultaneously. It has a surface + void location, and a subsurface + void location. Minions without voidwalk that enter the site will be banished. Spells cast from the surface + void location can target cards that are in the surface or the void, for example. Projectiles can travel from the surface + void location into the void.

title: FAQ: Thing in the Ice
text:
Q: What does 'can't be targeted or damaged by magic' mean?
A: Magic can't target the card and the card can't be damaged by Magic (even without targeting). The card can still be targeted by non-Magic effects.

title: FAQ: Thunderstorm
text:
Q: The alpha and beta text is different, which should I use?
A: The beta text is correct.

title: FAQ: Tide Naiads
text:
Q: Can Tide Naiads move from an underwater location to an underground location?
A: No. They would need to enter the underground location to flood it, and they cannot enter underground locations without burrowing.

title: FAQ: Toolbox
text:
Q: Can the bearer cast the spell, even if they're not a spellcaster?
A: Yes!

title: FAQ: Torrid Omphalos
text:
Q: Must spells cast by the Omphalos match its elements?
A: Yes. Any spell the Omphalos casts much match at least one of its elements.

title: FAQ: Torshammar Trinket
text:
Q: How does this work with end of turn and damage clearing?
A: The intent is that a 1 power minion with 1 damage + the Trinket would survive the turn.

title: FAQ: Trade Encampment
text:
Q: Do I have to reveal the traded artifacts?
A: Yes, you must reveal them to ensure it is a fair trade.

title: FAQ: Tringh Constrictor
text:
Q: The alpha and beta text is different, which should I use?
A: The beta text is correct.

title: FAQ: Troll Bridge
text:
Q: What is a 'lone enemy'?
A: A 'lone enemy' is an enemy unit that's not entering simultaneously with another enemy unit. Stationary units at the Troll Bridge ignored. Here are some examples: If an enemy [[War Horse]] is carrying its Avatar and moves to your Troll Bridge, it will not trigger, since there are two enemies entering simultaneously.  If your [[Bodach Bogeyman]] is carrying two enemy minions and moves to your Troll Bridge, it will not trigger. However, if the Bogeyman were carrying just one enemy, the Bridge would trigger. If there is already an enemy occupying the Troll Bridge and another enemy unit enters, it will trigger for the entering enemy.

title: FAQ: Truesight Crossbow
text:
Q: Can the bearer shoot or defend against a stealthed enemy?
A: Yes. The bearer can target stealthed minions with spells, shoot them with projectiles, attack or intercept them and even defend against their attacks.

title: FAQ: Tufted Turtles
text:
Q: My Tufted Turtles attack (having taken no damage so far this turn), and then 3 Foot Soldiers defend. How much damage do my Tufted Turtles take?
A: 0, because all three Foot Soldiers did damage at the same time, tied for first, and thus all are prevented!

title: FAQ: Twist of Fate
text:
Q: Does this count as healing?
A: No, this is setting life.

title: FAQ: Ultimate Horror
text:
Q: The alpha foil version has 3 air threshold and the normal version has 2 air threshold. Which is correct?
A: The normal version is correct. You only need 2 air affinity to cast this minion.

title: FAQ: Undertaker Engine
text:
Q: Can it burrow and unburrow different things the same turn?
A: Yes.

title: FAQ: Undertow
text:
Q: Does Undertow let you pull a unit underwater if they have submerge?
A: No, because it's a 'normal step,' which doesn't allow changing regions.

title: FAQ: Unland Angler
text:
Q: What are the details of pulling an oversized minion that occupies the water site and other locations?
A: When pulling or pushing a oversized unit, choose a single location the oversized unit occupies (and meets the requirement of the effect - e.g. adjacent), and push/pull from there.

title: FAQ: Unland Eel
text:
Q: When it submerges, can it pull down a minion anywhere in the realm, or only from its location?
A: No. Unland Eel can only drag a minion that shares its location.

title: FAQ: Vanguard Knights
text:
Q: If I have two Vanguard Knights equally forward, do they cancel each other out?
A: Yes. They only get the benefit if they are the true vanguard, with a single minion being the farthest forward.

title: FAQ: Varmint Warrens
text:
Q: Does this prevent enemy magic from harming my beasts?
A: Yes, as long as the effect says 'target'. You'll need to bring in a specialized exterminator to flush out these hidey-holes.

title: FAQ: Vatn Draconis
text:
Q: If I choose to submerge minions and artifacts here, do I submerge Vatn Draconis too?
A: Yes, it will submerge itself. You cannot choose to submerge only some of the minions and artifacts.

title: FAQ: Vaults of Zul
text:
Q: If I play this under my avatar, have I stopped there?
A: No, because a unit doesn't enter the site if the unit was already present in the square when the site was played.

title: FAQ: Vesper Swarm
text:
Q: What does it mean to 'fly to' something? Does it have to be the shortest possible path or any valid path?
A: Refer to the article on ((Moving to a Specific Location Via a Special Ability or Magic)) to see how an ability like this works.

title: FAQ: Vindictive Nation
text:
Q: When moving sites around, does Vindictive Nation protect the nearby sites before or after the move?
A: Vindictive Nation protects the sites it was nearby before the move. For example:  I = Vindictive Nation R = Rubble A = Allied Site My opponent casts Earthquake and rearranges the two rightmost sites:  Even though site A moved and is now nearby Vindictive Nation, my opponent doesn't lose any life because A wasn't nearby Vindictive Nation before the move. Alternately, if we started from the second situation and Earthquake moved sites into the first situation, my opponent would lose 3 life because they moved a site that was nearby Vindictive Nation (even though the site ended up no longer nearby).

title: FAQ: Vivien the Enchantress
text:
Q: What does 'wherever she is' mean?
A: Anywhere! The realm, your hand, and cemetery, and even while in the middle of your spellbook.

title: FAQ: Wall of Air
text:
Q: Does this affect subsurface units?
A: No. (They are not atop the site.)

title: FAQ: Wall of Fire
text:
Q: How many squares does this aura occupy?
A: 2

title: FAQ: Wall of Ice
text:
Q: How many squares does this aura occupy?
A: 2

title: FAQ: Warp Spasm
text:
Q: When is the power doubled?
A: This effect applies a doubling throughout the turn. If the unit gains or loses power, apply any additions or subtractions first, then double.

title: FAQ: Watchtower
text:
Q: What does it mean to 'permanently lose stealth'?
A: Simply remove the stealth token. It does not prevent the minion from gaining stealth later.

title: FAQ: Watery Grave
text:
Q: What does 'drowns' mean?
A: A minion 'drowns' if it dies due to being underwater without also having the submerge ability. You control the resulting Skeleton.

title: FAQ: Wave of Eviction
text:
Q: How do I properly resolve this effect?
A: Choose a cardinal direction from your water site. Forcefully move all enemies from your water site one step in the chosen direction and flood that site. Trigger and resolve any effects related to minions entering or the site being flooded. Then repeat the process until you reach the edge of the realm. The flood and push effect will continue even across a void, but minions cannot be forcefully moved across regions. Each site will be flooded at the same moment as the minions arrive, so a submerged minion being evicted will also be submerged on the new site (and there will never be a moment where it's pushed onto the new site without the new site also being flooded).

title: FAQ: Waveshaper
text:
Q: When exactly does the previous site stop being flooded when I use this ability for the second time?
A: The newly flooded site becomes flooded at the same moment the previously flooded site stops being flooded. If you choose the same site, there is no moment when the site isn't flood.

title: FAQ: Whirling Blades
text:
Q: Does the path include the starting and ending locations?
A: Yes.

title: FAQ: White Hart
text:
Q: Can the White Hart's location be attacked?
A: No, the White Hart's ability means that minions and locations which are nearby to the Hart, but are not the Hart, cannot be attacked. Everyone must focus on taking down the White Hart!

title: FAQ: Wildfire
text:
Q: Does 'visited before' apply to other Wildfires I cast in the same game?
A: Once it leaves play, a Wildfire forgets all the places it visited. If you have multiple Wildfires in play, track them each separately.

title: FAQ: Wills-o'-the-Wisp
text:
Q: If Wills-o'-the-Wisps are attacked and then use their ability to evade the attack, what happens?
A: Attack triggers are still satisfied (e.g. Captain Baldassare), but the attack otherwise ends (assuming there aren't any units left to fight). The attacker will not strike, and the target of the attack will not revert to the original target (if any).

title: FAQ: Windblast
text:
Q: Does the movement get resolved simultaneously?
A: Yes, all the steps are simultaneously resolved (which might then provoke a variety of triggers).

title: FAQ: Witherwing Hero
text:
Q: If a weaker ally is attacked and you return them to your hand via this ability, what happens?
A: Attack triggers are still satisfied (e.g. Captain Baldassare), but the attack otherwise ends, assuming there aren't any units left to fight. The attacker will not strike.

title: FAQ: Yog-Sothoth
text:
Q: What does 'Occupies all locations safely' mean?
A: Yog Sothoth occupies all locations simultaneously, in all regions. That includes all surface locations, subsurface locations and voids. Yog Sothoth does not die due to being burrowed or submerged and is not banished due to being in the void.

title: FAQ: Zephyranne Airship
text:
Q: What happens when a minion carries another minion that's carrying a minion?
A: Only the minions you're directly carrying count against your limit. Have fun at the carnival!

title: Codex: Abilities that Reference the Card's Own Name
text: There are many abilities that reference the name of the card which has the ability, either with the full name or part thereof. For example, [[Adept Illusionist]] and [[Locusts of Illyria]] both refer to their own name with their ability. When another card gains such an ability, the text should be read as referencing the new card's name. For instance, if both [[Adept Illusionist]] and [[Vivien the Enchantress]] are in play, Vivien can tap to search for another card named 'Vivien the Enchantress.' If [[Grigori Rasputin]] banishes and gains the abilities of [[Locusts of Illyria]], he will look to see if another card named 'Grigori Rasputin' has been summoned when creating a copy. In effect, when reading an ability which references the name of the card on which it is printed, you replace the name with a grammatically appropriate version of 'this card.'

title: Codex: Ability
